StackType.issue: Closed 2026-07-30 (tier-2 campaign): (Task 25.) The 15 `on_stack` no-op overrides are DELETED; the base `Power.on_stack` adds, matching PowerCmd.ModifyAmount (PowerCmd.cs:236), which adds unconditionally with no StackType branch -- PowerStackType.Single means 'Amount is hidden and displayed as 1' (PowerStackType.cs:10-13), not 'does not stack'. All 16 units re-verified against their own C#: 15 are StackType.Single, and NONE overrides InstanceType (PowerModel.cs:144 default None), so none needs T1's instance machinery instead of amount-adding. Two per-site exceptions, both verified: (1) DAMPEN's C# StackType is actually `None`, not Single (DampenPower.cs:22) -- the queue's 16-unit list was wrong about it; its only applier, MagiKnight, dedupes caller-side (MagiKnight.cs:78-96: re-application calls AddCaster only and never reaches PowerCmd.Apply), so the deletion is inert through the real caller and T28's caster-set machinery is untouched and re-pinned. (2) HEX genuinely reads Amount (HexPower.cs:79 feeds CardCmd.Afflict<Hexed>(card, Amount)), so this deletion closes a real divergence that remains DORMANT only because SpectralKnight's move machine never loops back to HEX and KnightsElite fields exactly one -- a second Hex applier makes it live. ILLUSION needed no override and is unchanged (the opposite-sign case the record notes). No reachable re-application among the other 13: Burrowed and Soar re-apply only after their own expire/remove, always onto a fresh instance. Pins: test/test_stack_type_single.py (39 tests).  The text it replaced read: The sim overrides on_stack to a no-op citing PowerStackType.Single, but Single only means 'Amount is hidden, and is always 1' (PowerStackType.cs:10-13) -- PowerCmd.ModifyAmount:236 adds the offset with no StackType branch. One of the 15 units making this misreading (`py audit/tools/power_census.py stack`). DORMANT for this unit: Amount is read nowhere in it, so the value is inert. Named trigger: any behaviour on this power that reads Amount. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.what: No preventer out-param on the sim's should_draw
guards.rationale: C#'s ShouldDraw is an AND predicate with first-False short-circuit (hook_dispatch step 35) and the sim's hooks.py has no preventer out-param, so which listener vetoed is unobservable. That absence is hook_dispatch's, not this unit's, and No Draw is currently the only ported should_draw listener, so no contention exists to observe.
